newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch court overturns Schiphol night-flight ban.
newsitem.headline: Dutch court overturns Schiphol night-flight ban.

text.p: The Haarlem district court on Friday prohibited restrictions on night flights at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport, Dutch news agency ANP reported.

Schiphol's ban, aimed at keeping noise levels at the airport within government-imposed limits, was being contested in court by the Dutch Air Transport Association (ATAN) and several individual airport users.

A court spokeswoman later confirmed the decision, saying the court had ruled that Schiphol was not authorised to impose the restrictions on night-time take-offs of noisier wide-body aircraft and the measures therefore had no legal validity.

"The court president has ordered Schiphol to withdraw the measures imposed...on August 5 to curb the (threatened) exceeding of noise limits within eight hours of the sentence being pronounced," the court said in a statement.
It said the only authority empowered to impose restrictions such as those envisaged by Schiphol was the transport minister, Annemarie Jorritsma.
Failure to comply with the court order would result in a fine of one million guilders ($481,000) per 24 hours up to a maximum of 10 million guilders, the court added.
Last Friday the court imposed an interim suspension on the night-flight ban pending today's judgement.
The ban, which prohibited take-offs of noisier wide-body aircraft from 2300-0600 hours local and unscheduled flights by all aircraft during those times, formally took hold on August 5.
However, under an initial period of grace aircraft had not physically been prevented from taking off but were instead issued with warnings.
ATAN had also sought a court injunction against the Dutch state to tolerate a temporary increase in noise levels above legal limits, but this request was turned down by the court.
"The claim against the State cannot be granted because the State has so far undertaken no action whatsoever in this case," the court said.

"If the State were still to act now, for example through the (transport) minister taking certain measures (her)self, then there would be legal administrative procedures to deal with the situation," it said. :
